recipes.name: Easy Corned Beef and Cabbage
ingredients_raw: 1 pound carrots, cut into large chunks
1 (3 pound) corned beef brisket with spice packet, cut in half
1 small head cabbage, cut into wedges

steps.text: Place potatoes, carrots, and onion into a 5-quart slow cooker. Combine water, sugar, vinegar, garlic, black pepper, bay leaf, and contents of spice packet in a small bowl; pour over vegetables. Top with beef brisket and cabbage.
Cover and cook on Low until beef and vegetables are tender, 8 to 9 hours. Remove bay leaf before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Corned Beef and Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: This corned beef recipe with cabbage is made in a slow cooker with potatoes and carrots for a quick and easy weeknight or St. Patrick's Day meal.

review.reviewBody: This is the first corned beef and cabbage recipe I have ever made. It was so good that I have no need to ever try another. Besides the fact that it was very easy to make, it tastes amazing! My boyfriend says it is his new favorite dish. The only thing I would recommend is to trim the majority of fat off of the brisket because it tends to either stay on the meat, or melt off into your vegetables.

This was one of the best recipes I've ever tried for corned beef. I liked the little hint of sweetness. I added brown sugar instead of white. I think 1-2 cups of water would be sufficient. I did not add the cabbage. I roasted that separately with onions in the oven, just because I like that better. I'm quite sure this will be my "go-to" recipe from now on for St. Patrick's Day!

I live at high altitude and I made this in my Instapot. It was wonderful! This will become a family recipe! I cooked a 4.5 lb corned beef for 7 hrs on the slow cooker selection, on high, with the warmer button off. I did NOT use the pressure cooker. I believe it was done in 5.2 hrs. I give this recipe a 9.5.

Excellent recipe. My family really enjoyed it, and it was so easy to make in the slow cooker. I substituted low sodium chicken broth for the water in the cooking liquid to add more flavor, and didn’t add the cabbage to the slow cooker as we don’t like it to be soggy- cooked it in my microwave steamer when the rest was done.

I discovered this recipe by accident. I've been making corned beef in the slow cooker now for several years. I'll not go back to boiling it - ever. In recent years, I've gone to steaming the veggies separately. So easy, so tasty. Thanks!
We loved it!! I used a little less water & added apple cider. Added potatoes the last 2 1/2 hrs. Excellent, easy, will make again!!!. Thank You!

Dynamite recipe!!! I used a 1 can of Bud Light and the rest with water. I also used a 4 pound Eye of Round Corned Beef Brisket which isn't that easy to find, but it has less fat, shrinks less, and is wonderful! It also doesn't fall apart. My guests couldn't stop raving about it. 
Normally this is a meal I reserve for St. Patty's Day, but I'll be having this several times throughout the year, thanks to this stress-free wonderful recipe!

Best corned beef and cabbage I have made yet! Great recipe and very easy! Didn't have apple cider vinegar but it still came out wonderful! I bought a 4 lb. brisket and quartered one red onion, this recipe had just the right amount of veggies (we love our veggies.) I cooked it on slow for 12 hours, the meat melted in our mouths, even the fatty part tasted good! Will be forwarding this recipe to family and friends, can't wait to make it again!

This came out so tender. I used a two pound brisket. I also added 1/2 a packet of dried onion soup mix because my family is allergic to sulfenic acid in onions. I added the cabbage during the last hour. It was amazing. I will be making this for Xmas Eve Dinner from now on. We are starting a new tradition

Served this last night to husband and guests. Delicious! This will be my go-to recipe for corned beef! The only thing I will change is to steam the cabbage separately to retain the pretty green color, as putting it in the crock-pot made it an ugly brown (Tasty though!) Thank you for this wonderful recipe!

I love this! It is the first time I have ever cooked corned beef. It was delicious! It was also very tender. My husband loved it. I cooked exactly as the directions stated. Also it was an excellent idea to add the cabbage at the last hour of cooking. I prefer a little spicy. So to change it up a bit cut the measurements in half for vinegar and sugar. Add jalapeno or habanero peppers. Use beef stock instead of water adds to the flavor. Viola! Delicious!
Added more carrots and onion also used beef broth
This is a Gr8 recipe meal 🍽️ for Saint Patrick’s Day. It’s a WINNER 🏆
Made this last night for the family and they seemed to like it. We have no LEFTOVERS!! This was my very first attempt at this dish and I must say that it is truly a "set and forget" dish!!!
Good bang for the effort makes this a keeper.
This is the exact same recipe I found on all recipes back in April 2010. I have use this recipe without any changes one or two times every year since. It’s easy and foolproof.

I would make this again. Easy to prepare, veggies came out perfect and meat was tender. I substituted half beef broth/half water and used brown sugar. I didn’t have bay leaves but everything still had good flavor.
Made for supper and came out delicious. I used little red potatoes and few carrots 🥕 I had on hand and cooked 9 hrs. Came out good. Eating good for couple days. Will make again
